issues.legal_issue: A magistrate may refer a complaint for police investigation before taking cognizance, where the allegations disclose a cognizable offence and investigation is an appropriate course.
material_facts: A social worker filed a complaint alleging that land had been purchased from a person who was already dead, and the complaint named several people, including public officials.
The magistrate heard the complainant’s counsel and considered the complaint and its supporting documents before directing the police to investigate and report.
The magistrate directed investigation before issuing process or otherwise taking cognizance of the alleged offence.
The accused sought to quash the proceedings, and the High Court declined to do so.
issues.conclusion: The magistrate acted within his power in directing a pre-cognizance police investigation, and the High Court was right to refuse to quash that direction; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 156(3) and 190 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an empowered magistrate may direct investigation before taking cognizance. If the magistrate takes cognizance and proceeds under Chapter XV, the magistrate cannot return to the pre-cognizance stage to use Section 156(3). A magistrate may choose police investigation where the complaint alleges a cognizable offence and referral would be conducive to justice, including by avoiding a judicial inquiry into a matter primarily for police investigation. The Court relied on CREF Finance Ltd. v. Shree Shanthi Homes (P) Ltd., Devarapalli Lakshminarayana Reddy v. V. Narayana Reddy, and Tula Ram v. Kishore Singh. Sections 200 and 190 and the procedures in Chapter XV govern the alternative course where the magistrate takes cognizance.

rule.if: challenge_to_pre_cognizance_investigation_order and empowered_magistrate and before_cognizance and cognizable_offence_alleged and investigation_conducive_to_justice

predicates.challenge_to_pre_cognizance_investigatio: The proceeding challenges a magistrate’s direction for police investigation made before deciding whether to take cognizance.
predicates.empowered_magistrate: The magistrate who made the direction was empowered to act on the complaint.
predicates.before_cognizance: The magistrate directed investigation before taking cognizance or beginning the post-cognizance complaint procedure.
predicates.cognizable_offence_alleged: The complaint alleged facts disclosing a cognizable offence.
predicates.investigation_conducive_to_justice: The magistrate considered police investigation an appropriate course, including because it could advance justice or avoid a judicial inquiry into a matter primarily for police investigation.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a pre-cognizance investigation direction, and an empowered magistrate directs investigation on allegations of a cognizable offence because investigation is conducive to justice, the direction is valid.
